reachweaver_live_status: As of 2026-10-15: one approved text post each was sent through ReachWeaver to Bluesky and Mastodon on 2026-10-11 (first-party receipts in docs/receipts/); Telegram/LinkedIn-member text adapters mock-tested only, with no live send; no other platform has a live receipt.

time_slot_policy.notes: Illustrative audience-local candidates. Not empirically established best times; compare matched-age results.

source_methodology: Native platform scheduling requires official documentation per non-unverified status. Market ordering is editorial hypothesis, never a claim about proprietary ranking or expected account reach. reviewed_on is the catalog edit date; each platform checked_on is its actual evidence date. Research-source homepages are not API or scheduler evidence. Nine India-focused entries were checked as candidate platform surfaces on 2026-10-15; website/help references do not establish account eligibility, native scheduling or publishing API access.

Author articles and discoverability controls; native scheduling unverified. The same Open API list names the Blog only as a search target and, through Naver Share, as a share destination; it lists no blog-writing API. Posting is a human act in the Naver editor; limits and the automation rule are unverified.

Individual cafe moderation and visibility rules govern posts. Naver's Open API list (read 2026-10-15) includes a login-method Cafe API that posts an article to a cafe board (POST /v1/cafe/{clubid}/menu/{menuid}/articles with a Naver Login access token). Scheduling, limits and the promotion rules of the cafe itself are unverified, and each cafe's own rules apply.

Opt-in groups only; no bulk invites, unsolicited chats or DM automation. The Kakao Developers documentation menu (read 2026-10-15) lists Kakao Talk Channel, Message, Share, Social and Push Notification products and no Open Chat API. The Kakao Customer Center rules page is JavaScript-only, so promotion and automation rules for Open Chat are unverified.

The owner's own Kakao Talk Channel (the business home on Kakao Talk), reaching people who added it as a friend; opt-in only. The Kakao Developers Channel API (read 2026-10-15) covers adding a channel, opening a 1:1 chat, and customer-group and relationship management for administrators, including sending targeted messages; it needs a Biz app connected to a Business Channel owned by the same business operator, and Kakao's review of a Business Channel takes about 3 to 5 business days. Message pricing, scheduling, limits and the automation and promotion rules are unverified, and the Kakao Customer Center pages are JavaScript-only.

LINE's Messaging API overview (read 2026-10-15) covers bots for LINE Official Accounts that reply to and message users who added the account as a friend, and does not mention OpenChat; no OpenChat posting API was found. The OpenChat guideline page is JavaScript-only, so its spam and promotion rules are unverified.

Anyone can use the API for free up to a monthly message allowance that depends on the account's subscription plan (the plan page is Japanese-only and was not read). Native scheduling, per-plan limits, media limits and the platform's automation and promotion rules are unverified.

Invite-only computing link aggregator. The about page keeps self-promotion to under a quarter of a member's activity and flags commercial promotion as spam; no posting API or scheduling is documented. Submitting is a human act by an established member.

Federated link aggregator run as separate instances. Post scheduling is a Lemmy 1.0 feature in open beta since 2026-05-19, so it depends on the instance version. Promotion rules are per instance and per community; lemmy.world's terms bar advertising bots.

Q&A network, not a place to announce projects. The Help Center (read 2026-10-15) says the community "tends to vote down overt self-promotion and flag it as spam" and that mentioning your own product requires disclosing your affiliation. The v2.3 API supports authenticated writes (the write_access scope, for example /questions/add) for applications registered on Stack Apps, under throttles; no scheduling is documented. Treated as human-only: a project announcement does not fit.

Per-repository forum: any authenticated user who can view a repository can post, and a GraphQL createDiscussion mutation exists. A maintainer announcement in your own repository's Discussions fits. The Acceptable Use Policies bar bulk promotion and inauthentic automated activity, so promotion in repositories you do not maintain is human-written only. No native scheduling is documented.

Hub Discussions on a repository, Posts (PRO accounts, one per day per the org page) and community articles (the Blog Explorers page says LLM-generated or low-quality articles are hidden from the blog). The Content Policy lists advertising and excessive bulk activity as spam. No scheduling is documented.

Public community workspaces. Users can schedule messages in the Slack apps and the API has chat.scheduleMessage, but whether a community lets an app or a promotion in is that community's admins' rule, and Slack's help centre says unsolicited promotions are against its Acceptable Use Policy.

Public Q&A and Spaces. Self-promotion is allowed only inside a sincere, direct answer, and repeated identical answers may be treated as spam. No official posting API or scheduling was found, and help.quora.com refused the research tools.

Blogging and reblogging network. Scheduling exists in the web editor and apps, and the v2 API can queue posts with publish_on. The User Guidelines, read through a search excerpt because the page needs JavaScript, forbid posting content automatically, systematically or programmatically.

German-speaking professional network. The XING Developer site (read 2026-10-15) lists only plugins: Share on XING, Login with XING and partner job integration; it lists no member posting API. The member terms page is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read, so the rules on promotion, automation and scheduling are unverified. Treated as human-only until they are read.

Newsletter platform: posts can be scheduled from the Review step of the post flow. The Create post API is available to publications on the Pro and Enterprise plans per the developer docs. The Acceptable Use Policy bars publications that rely entirely on AI-generated material and bots that simulate engagement.

Publishing and newsletter platform, self-hosted or Ghost(Pro). Posts can be scheduled in the editor and through the Admin API (status scheduled with a future published_at). The terms bar unsolicited promotion and accounts registered by bots; posting to your own site is not addressed.

Curation app. Content is added by hand or by an RSS feed submitted at flipboard.com/publishers and reviewed by staff; no posting API or scheduling was found. The Community Guidelines list high-volume automated posting and unapproved advertising as spam.

Video hosting. API upload needs approved upload access (reviewed by hand for developers without a paid plan, automatic on paid plans, per the help centre); no scheduled release for standard videos was found, and live-event scheduling is plan-limited. The Terms bar unauthorized automated access and ask for synthetic content to be labelled.

Live streaming. Streams can be scheduled in the Creator Dashboard or through the Helix Schedule API with the channel:manage:schedule scope; one-off segments are for partners and affiliates only. The Community Guidelines bar spam, botting and driving users to a livestream on another platform.

Creative portfolio community. The Community Guidelines list scripted or bulk automated uploading as a violation and expect authentic own work. The only API statement found is a 2021 Adobe reply that the API is unavailable, and Pro-plan scheduling is unverified because the help pages returned 403.

Design showcase and hiring community. Scheduling is documented only in the API (scheduled_for on shot creation, pro or team accounts, OAuth upload scope), and that documentation looks dated; Dribbble may refuse API access. The guidelines bar bots, advertising a product or service in shots and wholly AI-generated content.

Researcher network for publications, data and Q&A. No posting API or native scheduling is documented. The Terms and Community Guidelines returned 403 to the research tools, so the bot and self-promotion rules are unverified.

Messaging app. Channel superadmins can post through the Channels Post API to their own channel; the help centre's channel scheduling page returned 403, so scheduling is unverified. The Acceptable Use Policy bars spam, bulk and auto-messaging, and bots may message subscribers only.

markets.label: Worldwide / English baseline
markets.localization_note: No single worldwide posting time. Choose an actual target market before generating time slots.

markets.label: India pilot
markets.localization_note: English first for technical readers; human-review any Hindi material; subtitles never imply Hindi dictation support. Do not recommend TikTok without current local restrictions review: Indian government listed it as blocked in 2020 (https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1635206). Research additions checked 2026-10-15: Josh/Chingari/Hipi are candidate local-language short video; Public App is hyperlocal; Pratilipi is original storytelling; Rooter is gaming-only; Kutumb/LocalCircles and Arattai Channels require human-only, relevant, opt-in participation. These are platform-use hypotheses, not language support or ranking promises.
